cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: The Roman legion was the basic military unit of about 5,000 men, divided into 10 cohorts of 6 centuries of 80 men each

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: Legionaries carried a pilum (javelin) and gladius (short sword); the pilum's soft iron shank bent on impact, making shields unusable

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: Roman engineering: roads (over 400,000 km of roads connecting the empire), aqueducts (gravity-fed water supply), and fortifications like Hadrian's Wall

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: Hadrian's Wall (122 AD) was a 117 km defensive wall across northern Britain, marking the northwest frontier of the empire

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: Roman camps (castra) were built to a standard plan every night on campaign, with gates, roads and defences

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army & Engineering
cards.back: The army was also an engineering force: building roads, bridges, siege works and infrastructure wherever they went

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — the roman army & engineering?
cards.back: 1. For The Roman Army & Engineering, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with The Roman Army & Engineering 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
